steps.title: A boom
steps.body: In the 1990s, Merlot became the fashionable red in the US: soft, fruity and easy to pronounce. Plantings grew fast, often in hot, high-yield sites, giving bland, simple wines. Quality became uneven, and the name grew associated with mass-market wine.

steps.title: Sideways
steps.body: In the 2004 film Sideways, the main character declares he won't drink Merlot. US Merlot sales growth slowed, while Pinot Noir sales rose. Ironically, his treasured bottle is a 1961 Cheval Blanc, a Saint-Émilion with a large share of Merlot alongside Cabernet Franc.

steps.prompt: What wine does the main character of Sideways treasure?
steps.explanation: The irony is that Cheval Blanc contains a large share of Merlot.

steps.title: Great Merlot endures
steps.body: Merlot makes some of the world's most expensive wines: Pétrus, Le Pin, Masseto in Tuscany. Washington State, Hawke's Bay and parts of Chile make excellent, fresh Merlot. Quality depends on site, yield and picking time, like any grape. The backlash was about overproduction, not the grape.

steps.explanation: Sancerre is Sauvignon Blanc from the Loire.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Merlot boomed in the 1990s, often overproduced
Great Merlot, from Pétrus to Masseto, endures
